# Popularity Model Results

*Generated by `src/model.py`. All numbers come from the run; nothing is typed in.*

## Target definition

**Popularity class = within-country tertiles (thirds) of votes among rated restaurants (Low / Medium / High). Unrated restaurants have no class and are not used for training.** Votes, aggregate rating, rating text, rating colour and the rated flag are excluded as model features because the target is built from votes; a model that uses them is invalid (leaky).

## Setup

- Target: `popularity_class` (Option B: within-country tertiles of votes), rated restaurants only (n = 7,403). Unrated restaurants are excluded.
- Split: 80/20 stratified, random_state = 42 (train 5,922, test 1,481).
- Tuning: 5-fold stratified CV on the training set, scored by macro-F1. Best model chosen by CV score, then evaluated once on the test set.
- Features (34): country, city_group, price_range, cost_pct_in_country, is_cost_outlier, has_table_booking, has_online_delivery, is_delivering_now, n_cuisines, latitude, longitude, has_valid_coords, log_branch_count, log_locality_size, cuisine_north_indian, cuisine_chinese, cuisine_fast_food, cuisine_mughlai, cuisine_italian, cuisine_bakery, cuisine_continental, cuisine_cafe, cuisine_desserts, cuisine_south_indian, cuisine_street_food, cuisine_american, cuisine_pizza, cuisine_mithai, cuisine_burger, cuisine_thai, cuisine_asian, cuisine_beverages, cuisine_ice_cream, cuisine_mexican.
- **Excluded (leakage):** votes, aggregate_rating, rating_text, rating_color, is_rated, votes_pct_in_country and any aggregate of votes or rating. Checked in code by `assert_no_leakage`.

## Model comparison

| model | cv_f1_macro_mean | cv_f1_macro_std | test_accuracy | test_precision_macro | test_recall_macro | test_f1_macro | test_f1_weighted | test_roc_auc_ovr_macro |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline (majority class) | 0.167 | 0.000 | 0.336 | 0.112 | 0.333 | 0.168 | 0.169 | 0.500 |
| Logistic Regression | 0.555 | 0.014 | 0.550 | 0.541 | 0.549 | 0.543 | 0.543 | 0.732 |

| Random Forest | 0.578 | 0.008 | 0.581 | 0.571 | 0.580 | 0.573 | 0.574 | 0.768 |
| Gradient Boosting | 0.624 | 0.012 | 0.613 | 0.609 | 0.612 | 0.611 | 0.611 | 0.795 |

**Best model (by CV macro-F1): Gradient Boosting**, with test accuracy 0.613, macro-F1 0.611 and ROC-AUC 0.795. The majority-class baseline scores accuracy 0.336. For comparison, a model that is allowed to see votes and rating scores much higher (see *Leakage demonstration* below), but that score is not valid.

Hyper-parameters chosen:

- Baseline (majority class): `{}`
- Logistic Regression: `{"C": 10.0}`
- Decision Tree: `{"max_depth": 12, "min_samples_leaf": 20}`
- Random Forest: `{"max_depth": 16, "min_samples_leaf": 1}`
- Gradient Boosting: `{"learning_rate": 0.1, "max_depth": 3, "n_estimators": 300}`

## Important caveat: uneven sampling by location

Location features rank highest. The share of each popularity class differs strongly by zone:

| zone | Low % | Medium % | High % | rated restaurants | median votes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| India: Delhi NCR | 37.4 | 33.9 | 28.7 | 5,808 | 40 |
| India: other cities | 2.4 | 25.5 | 72.1 | 705 | 191 |
| Outside India | 32.9 | 33.3 | 33.8 | 890 | 208 |

Outside Delhi NCR, Zomato appears to list only a small set of well-known (highly voted) restaurants per Indian city, so the model can partly learn *where* a restaurant was sampled. This is not leakage (location is a legitimate input), but it could inflate the score. Robustness checks with the same algorithm and hyper-parameters:

| variant | rows | features | test accuracy | test macro-F1 | test ROC-AUC | majority baseline accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Main model (all rated, all features) | 7,403 | 34 | 0.613 | 0.611 | 0.795 | 0.336 |
| Delhi NCR only (consistent sampling) | 5,808 | 34 | 0.614 | 0.614 | 0.790 | 0.374 |
| All rated, location features removed | 7,403 | 28 | 0.519 | 0.514 | 0.715 | 0.336 |

Interpretation: within Delhi NCR alone, where sampling is consistent, macro-F1 is 0.614, about the same as the main model (0.611), so the main result is not mainly explained by the sampling pattern. Removing all location features lowers macro-F1 to 0.514 (still above the baseline), so *where* a restaurant is (down to locality) carries real signal, and price, services, cuisines and chain status add signal of their own.

## Leakage demonstration (illustration only)

Same Gradient Boosting hyper-parameters and the same 80/20 split (random_state = 42), but with `votes` and `aggregate_rating` added to the 34 features. This model is **not valid** and is never saved or used: the target is built from votes, so the inputs already contain the answer, which would not be known for a new restaurant.

| model | features | test accuracy | test macro-F1 | test ROC-AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gradient Boosting (honest, 34 features) | 34 | 0.613 | 0.611 | 0.795 |
| Leaky model (illustration only): + votes, aggregate_rating | 36 | 0.988 | 0.988 | 1.000 |

Adding the two leaked columns raises test accuracy from 61.3% to 98.8% (macro-F1 0.611 -> 0.988). The jump measures the leak, not real predictive skill.

## Predictions file (Power BI page 4)

`outputs/predictions/popularity_predictions.csv`: 7,403 rated restaurants. Test rows are predicted by the final model; training rows use out-of-fold (cross-validated) predictions, so no restaurant is predicted by a model that was trained on it. Overall agreement: 62.4%.

## Model variants (one comparison table)

Same algorithm and hyper-parameters as the main model; only rows and features change. Each variant has its own stratified 80/20 split (random_state 42).

| variant | valid | rows | features | CV macro-F1 (train) | test accuracy | test macro-F1 | test ROC-AUC | majority baseline acc. | top 3 features (drop in macro-F1) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Main (all countries, all features) | yes | 7,403 | 34 | 0.624 | 0.613 | 0.611 | 0.795 | 0.336 | latitude (0.077); city_group (0.073); cost_pct_in_country (0.060) |
| No location (all countries) | yes | 7,403 | 28 | 0.542 | 0.519 | 0.514 | 0.715 | 0.336 | cost_pct_in_country (0.065); has_online_delivery (0.030); price_range (0.024) |
| India, with city/locality | yes | 6,513 | 33 | 0.636 | 0.625 | 0.622 | 0.802 | 0.336 | cost_pct_in_country (0.067); longitude (0.066); has_online_delivery (0.042) |
| India, without city/locality | yes | 6,513 | 28 | 0.561 | 0.572 | 0.569 | 0.748 | 0.336 | cost_pct_in_country (0.129); price_range (0.088); has_online_delivery (0.051) |
| Baseline (majority class) | yes | 7,403 | 34 | 0.167 | 0.336 | 0.168 | 0.500 | 0.336 | - |
| Leaky: + votes and rating (INVALID) | NO (leakage) | 7,403 | 36 | 0.991 | 0.988 | 0.988 | 1.000 | 0.336 | votes (0.661); country (0.086); longitude (0.011) |

Features removed per variant:

- **Main (all countries, all features)**: none
- **No location (all countries)**: country, city_group, latitude, longitude, has_valid_coords, log_locality_size
- **India, with city/locality**: country
- **India, without city/locality**: country, city_group, latitude, longitude, has_valid_coords, log_locality_size
- **Baseline (majority class)**: n/a (always predicts the most common class)
- **Leaky: + votes and rating (INVALID)**: none; votes and aggregate_rating ADDED

Removing location lowers macro-F1 from 0.611 to 0.514 (all countries) and from 0.622 to 0.569 (India only). The leaky variant reaches 98.8% accuracy only because votes are both input and target; it is not a valid result.

## Medium class: honest improvement attempts

Tuned on the training set only (5-fold CV / out-of-fold predictions); each approach evaluated once on the same test set. The saved main model is not replaced.

| method | tuned on training set | CV macro-F1 (train) | test accuracy | test macro-F1 | test ROC-AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before: main model (highest probability) | - | 0.624 | 0.613 | 0.611 | 0.795 |
| Class weights (Medium up-weighted) | Medium weight = 1 (grid [1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0]) | 0.624 | 0.613 | 0.611 | 0.795 |
| Threshold tuning (Medium bias) | Medium bias = +0.03 (grid -0.10 to +0.30) | 0.625 | 0.604 | 0.604 | 0.795 |
| Ordinal (Frank and Hall) | - | 0.619 | 0.621 | 0.621 | 0.802 |

Note: the CV score of threshold tuning is slightly optimistic, because the bias was chosen on the same out-of-fold predictions; its test score is not affected.

Per-class precision and recall, before and after (test set):

| method | class | precision | recall | F1 | support |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before: main model (highest probability) | Low | 0.655 | 0.662 | 0.659 | 497 |
| Before: main model (highest probability) | Medium | 0.503 | 0.472 | 0.487 | 489 |
| Before: main model (highest probability) | High | 0.669 | 0.703 | 0.686 | 495 |
| Class weights (Medium up-weighted) | Low | 0.655 | 0.662 | 0.659 | 497 |
| Class weights (Medium up-weighted) | Medium | 0.503 | 0.472 | 0.487 | 489 |
| Class weights (Medium up-weighted) | High | 0.669 | 0.703 | 0.686 | 495 |
| Threshold tuning (Medium bias) | Low | 0.655 | 0.638 | 0.646 | 497 |
| Threshold tuning (Medium bias) | Medium | 0.486 | 0.495 | 0.490 | 489 |
| Threshold tuning (Medium bias) | High | 0.671 | 0.677 | 0.674 | 495 |
| Ordinal (Frank and Hall) | Low | 0.674 | 0.652 | 0.663 | 497 |
| Ordinal (Frank and Hall) | Medium | 0.502 | 0.515 | 0.509 | 489 |
| Ordinal (Frank and Hall) | High | 0.691 | 0.695 | 0.693 | 495 |

Medium F1 before: 0.487 (recall 0.472). Chosen by training CV macro-F1: Threshold tuning (Medium bias) (CV 0.625 vs 0.624 before), test Medium F1 0.490. Highest test Medium F1: Ordinal (Frank and Hall) (0.509); this was not the CV choice, so it is reported but not selected (choosing by test score would overfit the test set).

## Why Medium is hard: it borders both other classes

The target cuts each country's rated restaurants at the 1/3 and 2/3 percentiles of votes. Medium is the middle third, so every Medium restaurant is at most 16.7 percentile points from a cut-off, while Low and High restaurants can be up to 33.3 points away.

Vote ranges per class and cut-offs (cut-off = midpoint between neighbouring classes):

| country | rated | Low votes | Medium votes | High votes | cut-off Low/Medium | cut-off Medium/High |

| India | 6,513 | 4-24 | 25-99 | 100-10934 | 24.5 | 99.5 |
| United States | 431 | 6-160 | 161-465 | 467-3157 | 160.5 | 466 |
| United Kingdom | 79 | 9-63 | 64-213 | 214-1326 | 63.5 | 213.5 |
| UAE | 60 | 12-228 | 246-449 | 459-2510 | 237 | 454 |
| South Africa | 60 | 20-157 | 158-328 | 356-1207 | 157.5 | 342 |
| Brazil | 55 | 5-9 | 10-22 | 24-73 | 9.5 | 23 |
| New Zealand | 40 | 31-133 | 141-223 | 229-754 | 137 | 226 |
| Turkey | 34 | 72-115 | 123-522 | 591-1311 | 119 | 556.5 |
| Australia | 24 | 11-29 | 31-97 | 100-381 | 30 | 98.5 |
| Philippines | 22 | 29-270 | 294-488 | 520-1070 | 282 | 504 |
| Indonesia | 21 | 22-331 | 395-873 | 903-2212 | 363 | 888 |
| Qatar | 20 | 41-83 | 109-182 | 189-350 | 96 | 185.5 |

Distance to the nearest cut-off, by class (all rated restaurants; 'near' = within 10 votes):

## Separate question: High vs Low only (2 classes, Medium excluded)

**This is not the 3-class result.** It answers a different, easier question: can the model tell a clearly popular restaurant (top third) from a clearly unpopular one (bottom third)? Medium restaurants are removed before the split, so its accuracy must not be compared with the 3-class accuracy.

- Rows: 4,957 (train 3,965, test 992); same features and hyper-parameters as the main model; stratified 80/20, random_state 42.
- CV macro-F1 (train): 0.865. Test accuracy 0.832, macro-F1 0.832, ROC-AUC 0.925. Majority baseline accuracy 0.501.

| class | precision | recall | F1 | support |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low | 0.844 | 0.815 | 0.829 | 497 |
| High | 0.820 | 0.848 | 0.834 | 495 |

| actual \ predicted | Low | High |
|---|---|---|
| Low | 405 | 92 |
| High | 75 | 420 |
